title: À la recherche de Sofia  (Looking for Sofia)

segments.t: At a lavish Cannes Film Festival party, Gabriel is searching frantically for Sofia. Meanwhile, Hicham catches up with Camille and tries to lure her back to the agency with an exciting offer. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Gabriel, j'ai à te parler.
Pas maintenant, Camille!
Guy veut que je sois son agent.
Super, mais tu as vu Sofia?
Elle parlait avec France 2 tout à l'heure.
Tu cherches quelqu'un, Gabriel?
Oui, je cherche désespérément Sofia.
Camille, tu devrais revenir chez ASK.
C'est très gentil, Hicham.
J'ai vraiment besoin d'une assistante.
C'est Mathias qui a plaidé ta cause.
Je préfère partir à New York avec Andréa.
Travailler pour cette agence américaine?
Oui, l'agence s'appelle UBA.
C'est une opportunité très tentante.
Let's walk through Gabriel's search across the party step by step.
Gabriel, j'ai à te parler.
'Gabriel, I need to talk to you.' Compact 'I have to speak' with 'to you' tucked in front is a brisk expression in French for 'I need to talk to you.'
Pas maintenant, Camille!
'Not now, Camille!' Two blunt words—'not now'—work word for word in French when someone is in a rush.
Guy veut que je sois son agent.
'Guy wants me to be his agent.' After 'wants that,' French switches 'am' to its wish-form 'be'—literally 'wants that I be his agent.'
Super, mais tu as vu Sofia?
'Great, but have you seen Sofia?' International 'super!' opens the reply, followed by 'you have seen Sofia?' with rising pitch in French.
Elle parlait avec France 2 tout à l'heure.
'She was talking with France 2 earlier.' Notice that the exact same three-word chunk meaning 'see you later' ALSO means 'just earlier today' when paired with a past action in French!
Tu cherches quelqu'un, Gabriel?
'Are you looking for someone, Gabriel?' Unlike English 'look for,' French packs 'for' right inside 'seek'—so no extra preposition is needed before 'someone'!
Oui, je cherche désespérément Sofia.
'Yes, I am desperately looking for Sofia.' Long adverb 'desperately' sits right after 'seek' in French, built by adding '-ment' onto 'desperate.'
Camille, tu devrais revenir chez ASK.
'Camille, you should come back to ASK.' Built from 'come' with 're-,' 'come back' pairs with 'at the home of' before company name ASK in French.
C'est très gentil, Hicham.
'That is very kind, Hicham.' Everyday 'nice/kind' is a warm polite brush-off in French when someone appreciates an offer she plans to decline.
J'ai vraiment besoin d'une assistante.
'I really need an assistant.' Putting 'really' between 'have' and 'need of' gives Hicham's pitch extra sincerity in French.
C'est Mathias qui a plaidé ta cause.
'Mathias is the one who pleaded your case.' Framing 'Mathias' inside 'it is... who' spotlights him, followed by the courtroom expression 'pleaded your cause' in French.
Je préfère partir à New York avec Andréa.
'I prefer going to New York with Andrea.' After 'prefer' in French, 'leave/depart' attaches directly without any preposition, followed by 'to New York.'
Travailler pour cette agence américaine?
'Working for that American agency?' Leading with bare 'to work' as an echoed question fragment sounds completely natural in French.
Oui, l'agence s'appelle UBA.
'Yes, the agency is called UBA.' Literally 'the agency calls itself UBA'—how French always states the name of a person, pet, or company!
C'est une opportunité très tentante.

'It is a very tempting opportunity.' Notice 'opportunity very tempting' putting the '-ant' description after the noun in French. Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Gabriel, j'ai à te parler.
Pas maintenant, Camille!
Guy veut que je sois son agent.
Super, mais tu as vu Sofia?
Elle parlait avec France 2 tout à l'heure.
Tu cherches quelqu'un, Gabriel?
Oui, je cherche désespérément Sofia.
Camille, tu devrais revenir chez ASK.
C'est très gentil, Hicham.
J'ai vraiment besoin d'une assistante.
C'est Mathias qui a plaidé ta cause.
Je préfère partir à New York avec Andréa.
Travailler pour cette agence américaine?
Oui, l'agence s'appelle UBA.
C'est une opportunité très tentante.
While Gabriel frantically hunts for Sofia across the crowded Cannes party, Camille and Hicham discuss her exciting prospects with an American agency. See you next time!
À demain!
